input.quote: (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services)
input.rationale: §5a imposes a minimum monthly fee floor for Hosting Services and Support Services, so the preferred position (no minimum commitment; pay only for usage or ordered services) is not met. The bargain does, however, sit at the fallback on its material terms: (i) the commitment runs only for the current 12-month term — §13 sets a 1-year term that continues only if neither party gives 30 days' notice of intent not to renew, so there is no multi-year lock-in; (ii) Client has an exit on short notice — §14 lets Client terminate by an unconditional written election, with services (and therefore the fee floor) ending the last day of the month following notice; and (iii) the floor operates as a true-up (Client pays the greater of actual charges or the monthly minimum) with no shortfall penalty, liquidated damages or accelerated-balance mechanic anywhere in the document. Per the playbook, a clause at the fallback is accepted and not redlined. Two minor points for the rationale only, not redlined: the §14 exit takes effect at month-end following notice (up to ~60 days) rather than a flat 30 days, and the minimum amounts in §5a (and the Support Services period in §4) remain blank — we should confirm those figures commercially before signature. Note also that §3(i)'s per-borrower credit-report ordering obligation applies only where Client voluntarily uses the Interface, and §2a expressly leaves Client free to use alternatives, so it is not a volume commitment or usage cap under this rule; the non-renewal mechanic in §13 belongs to RENEWAL and is not flagged here.
